fields.Volume: ~300–600 ratings per month (upper-bounded by completed projects per W4997 at realistic response rates)

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-solicit on completion; review-authenticity detection; auto-aggregate to scorecard; ranking feed
Controls: - CTL-748 (ensure controlled execution — Network Performance, Quality, Compliance & Analytics (PA-172.3).)
- CTL-748: ratings solicited post-completion; reviews authentic; consent respected; scorecard updated
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX/W65), VS-91 (privacy), VS-125 (fake-review), VS-95 (marketplace), W4990 (profile), W4994 (ranking), W4998 (completion), W5002 (scorecard)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-response risk**: Few ratings → weak signal; mitigated by prompt solicitation and incentives
- **Fake-review risk**: Inauthentic reviews mislead (VS-125); mitigated by authenticity controls
- **Bias/manipulation risk**: Reviews manipulated against/for installers; mitigated by governance

steps.activity: Solicit the rating/feedback: post-completion (W4998), request the customer rate the installer/work (CSAT/NPS, workmanship, timeliness, professionalism, value) via the platform/app/SMS (links VS-13 W65)

Manage reviews & authenticity: publish reviews on the installer profile (W4990) per consent, verify authenticity (prevent fake/retaliatory reviews — links VS-125), and manage the installer's right-of-reply
Analyze & act: aggregate ratings into the scorecard (W5002), identify low-rated installers for review/improvement (W5005), and feed CX analytics and the Find-a-Pro ranking (W4994)

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), CX (VS-13), Quality (VS-31), Network Manager, Installer

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-build of "Build the scorecard: per-installer KPIs" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-rank of "rank within trade/area, identify top/bottom performers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "improvement plans for under-performers" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-748 (ensure controlled execution — Network Performance, Quality, Compliance & Analytics (PA-172.3).)
- CTL-748: multi-dimensional scorecard; reviewed monthly; top/bottom acted on; tiers managed
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-31 (quality), VS-67/VS-133 (improvement), W4989 (tier), W5001 (rating), W5003/W5004 (quality/warranty), W5005 (removal), W5006 (compliance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-gaming risk**: Installers gaming KPIs; mitigated by balanced multi-dimensional scorecard
- **Inaction risk**: Scorecard not actioned → poor performers retained; mitigated by tier/removal process
- **Unfairness risk**: Scorecard penalizes installers unfairly; mitigated by transparency and right-of-reply
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); CX (VS-13); quality (VS-31); marketplace (VS-95); CRM (VS-11); scorecard platform

steps.activity: Build the scorecard: per-installer KPIs — rating (W5001), response/quote/completion time, acceptance rate, completion verification (W4998), quality/defect (W5003/W5004), complaints (W5005), compliance (W5006), and referral-fee/revenue contribution
Review & rank: review the scorecard per installer, rank within trade/area, identify top/bottom performers, and manage tiers (W4989) and preferred status
Act on performance: recognition for top performers, improvement plans for under-performers (links VS-67/VS-133 improvement), tier changes, and removal (W5005) for persistent poor performance

workflows.name: Quality Assurance, Workmanship Inspection & Site Audit

Automation Opportunity: - Inspection-checklist app; photo-evidence capture; risk-based audit targeting; defect→warranty auto-feed
Controls: - CTL-748: QA standards defined; inspections conducted; defects remediated; scorecard updated
Cross-references: - links to VS-31 (quality), VS-117 (standards/code), VS-22 (compliance), VS-24 (HSE), W5002 (scorecard), W5004 (warranty), W5005 (improvement/removal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Defect risk**: Poor workmanship → warranty/disputes/customer harm (VS-53/W5004); mitigated by QA
- **Code-violation risk**: Work not to building/trade code (links VS-117/VS-22); mitigated by standard-aligned inspection
- **Sampling-gap risk**: Risk-based sample misses systemic issues; mitigated by analytics-driven targeting
System Touchpoints: - Quality (VS-31); standards/cert (VS-117); HSE (VS-24); inspection platform/analytics (VS-28); marketplace (VS-95)

steps.activity: Define QA standards: the workmanship standard per trade (aligned to trade/building code — links VS-117 DTI-BPS, VS-31 quality), the inspection criteria/checklist, and the sampling/risk-based audit plan
Conduct inspections/audits: site inspection of completed/in-progress work (sample + risk-based), documentation (photo/checklist), verify compliance to standard/code, and identify defects (W5004)
Act on findings: defect remediation (W5004), scorecard impact (W5002), improvement/removal (W5005), and feed quality analytics/standards improvement

workflows.name: Warranty, Defect Liability & Post-Installation Service Obligation

Automation Opportunity: - Claim intake/workflow; defect-liability tracking; cost-recovery from retention; scorecard feed
Controls: - CTL-748 (ensure controlled execution — Network Performance, Quality, Compliance & Analytics (PA-172.3).)
- CTL-748: warranty terms in agreement; claims tracked to resolution; cost recovered; scorecard updated
Cross-references: - links to VS-53 (warranty), VS-116 (bond/retention), VS-31 (quality), VS-100 (legal), W4989 (agreement), W5000 (alternate), W5002 (scorecard), W5003 (QA), W5005 (disputes)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uncovered-defect risk**: No warranty/defect-liability → customer bears cost/harm; mitigated by warranty terms
- **Installer-non-remediation risk**: Installer won't fix → customer harm; mitigated by retention/bond and alternate remediation
- **Cost-recovery risk**: Remediation cost not recovered from installer; mitigated by retention/bond mechanism
System Touchpoints: - Warranty (VS-53); quality (VS-31); CX (VS-13); finance (VS-17/VS-16); legal (VS-100); surety/bond (VS-116)

steps.activity: Define warranty/defect-liability terms: the workmanship warranty period/scope per trade (in the installer agreement W4989), the materials warranty (links VS-53 product warranty), and the defect-liability/retention mechanism

Manage claims: receive the customer defect/warranty claim, diagnose (workmanship vs materials vs customer), assign remediation to the installer (or alternate W5000), and track to resolution (links VS-53)
Recover cost & learn: recover remediation cost from the installer (retention/bond/fee per agreement), feed the scorecard (W5002) and QA (W5003), and manage disputes (W5005)

workflows.name: Dispute Resolution, Complaint Handling & Installer Discipline/Removal

Automation Opportunity: - Complaint-triage workflow; case-management; due-process tracking; removal-with-audit-trail
Controls: - CTL-748 (ensure controlled execution — Network Performance, Quality, Compliance & Analytics (PA-172.3).)
- CTL-748: disputes investigated & resolved; remediation/recovery; discipline with due process; removal documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX/complaints), VS-100 (legal), VS-119 (ethics), VS-31 (quality), W4992 (code-of-conduct), W5000 (alternate), W5002 (scorecard), W5004 (warranty)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unresolved-dispute risk**: Disputes unresolved → customer/legal escalation (VS-100); mitigated by resolution framework
- **Unfair-discipline risk**: Installer removed without due process → grievance/legal; mitigated by due process
- **Recurrence risk**: Poor installer retained → repeat harm; mitigated by discipline/removal
System Touchpoints: - CX/complaints (VS-13); legal (VS-100); ethics (VS-119); quality (VS-31); finance (VS-17); marketplace (VS-95)

steps.activity: Triage & investigate the dispute: receive the complaint (links VS-13), triage (workmanship/pricing/conduct/timeliness), investigate (evidence, both parties), and determine cause/responsibility
Resolve: mediate customer↔installer resolution, remediation (W5004), refund/compensation where warranted, alternate installer (W5000), and customer recovery (VS-13)

Discipline/remove: for installer fault/conduct breach (W4992), apply discipline (warning/suspension/fee), remove from the network for serious/recurrent breach (with due process/Legal VS-100), and document

fields.Volume: Quarterly compliance monitoring across the ~300–500-installer network

Automation Opportunity: - License/insurance register auto-verify; expiration alerts; suspension-on-lapse gate; sanctions re-screen (VS-86)

Cross-references: - links to VS-165 (PCAB), VS-166 (license portfolio), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-86 (sanctions), VS-26 (insurance), W4987 (vetting), W5002 (scorecard), W5005 (removal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapse risk**: Installer license/insurance lapses → illegal referral/liability (RA 4566); mitigated by continuous monitoring and suspension-on-lapse

steps.activity: Continuously monitor licenses/insurance: track PCAB license (RA 4566 — links VS-165), trade licenses, insurance, permits for expiration/lapse, verify against official registers, and alert on lapse (links VS-166 license portfolio)
Re-verify periodically: periodic re-verification of license/insurance/financial standing (links W4987/W4988), sanctions/ethics re-screen (VS-86/VS-119), and quality re-assessment (W5003)
Act on lapse/non-compliance: suspend referrals on lapse, require remediation/reactivation, remove for serious lapse (W5005), and feed the scorecard (W5002) and TPRM (VS-161)

Recommend & prioritize: improvements to coverage (W4991), economics (W4985/W4997), quality/compliance (W5003/W5006), and platform/UX (W4990); feed strategy and the leadership review
